id: 2f8c5a7d-9b3e-4c1f-a5d8-7e4f9b2c3d66
status: experimental
description: Detects bun.exe (or node.exe carrying the Bun payload) making outbound HTTPS to npm publish, PyPI upload, or GitHub repo/gist creation endpoints — the Miasma/Hades worm spreading and exfiltration channels.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  dest:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'registry.npmjs.org'
      - 'upload.pypi.org'
      - 'api.github.com'
  condition: proc and dest
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\BUN.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) @DestinationHostname:(registry.npmjs.org OR upload.pypi.org OR api.github.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(bun|node)\.exe$/i
| DomainName=/^(registry\.npmjs\.org|upload\.pypi\.org|api\.github\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| count>0
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(All_Traffic.url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe" AND (All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish*" OR All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/user*" OR All_Traffic.url="*upload.pypi.org/legacy/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/user/repos*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/contents/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/git/refs*") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Traffic.url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe" AND (All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/publish*" OR All_Traffic.url="*registry.npmjs.org/-/user*" OR All_Traffic.url="*upload.pypi.org/legacy/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/user/repos*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/contents/*" OR All_Traffic.url="*api.github.com/repos/*/git/refs*") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'

falsepositives:

level: critical

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution

Medium

Rust Clipboard Hijacker Uses Fake GitHub Stars and VirusTotal Upvotes to Steal Crypto

Cyber Security News
2026-06-18 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

A newly discovered malware campaign is quietly draining cryptocurrency wallets by doing something most security tools never see coming. Instead of relying on brute-force attacks or dark web exploits, the threat actor behind this campaign built a fake reputation engine across multiple platforms to make dangerous software look completely safe and trustworthy. The malware at [&#8230;] The post Rust Clipboard Hijacker Uses Fake GitHub Stars and VirusTotal Upvotes to Steal Crypto appeared first on Cyber Security News .

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — From package to postinstall payload: Inside the Mastra npm supply chain compromi
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mastra npm supply chain: easy-day-js postinstall dropper (node setup.cjs --no-warnings) · [LLM] Mastra implant Windows persistence: NvmProtocal Run key + NodePackages drop · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Mastra C2 beacon: node.exe to Hostwinds 23.254.164.92:8000 / .123:443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mastra implant credential access: node.exe reading crypto wallet extensions / browser History · [LLM] Mastra implant discovery: PowerShell child of node.exe running Get-StartApps / Get-AppxPackage · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Mastra npm supply chain: easy-day-js postinstall dropper (node setup.cjs --no-warnings) AIInstallation High
Detects the easy-day-js@1.11.22 postinstall hook spawning the obfuscated setup.cjs dropper via Node.js with the --no-warnings flag. This is the entry point execution on any developer workstation or CI/CD runner that resolved the poisoned mastra/@mastra packages. Rationale: Anchors on the exact strings published by Microsoft for the malicious postinstall — node binary spawning setup.cjs with --no-warnings (Block 1 of the article). Also restricts the parent to npm/node/yarn/pnpm lineage to slash FPs from unrelated scripts that share the filename. Cross-referenced the mastra GitHub issue 18046 which confirms the postinstall hook in easy-day-js@1.11.22. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046 • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/microsoft-threat-intelligence_microsoft-has-identified-a-supply-chain-attack-activity
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal npm package whose postinstall is also named setup.cjs and invokes node --no-warnings (rare — the dual-string match makes this unlikely)
  • Developer manually testing/reverse-engineering the malicious dropper after the campaign was disclosed
  • A CI/CD job that intentionally runs a script literally called setup.cjs with warnings suppressed
  • Security tooling (EDR sandbox, npm audit replays) that re-executes the dropper for analysis
Suppression filter
| where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4","c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638","cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066","9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9","221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or FolderPath has @"\node_modules\easy-day-js\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree on the host (parent npm/yarn → node setup.cjs); collect the SHA256 of the setup.cjs file and compare to the five published hashes; check $TMPDIR for .pkg_history and .pkg_logs markers. 2) Contain: isolate the host or CI runner from network, kill node tree, quarantine node_modules/easy-day-js, rotate every credential / token / SSH key / cloud key that touched that machine since 2026-06-16 07:05 UTC. 3) Hunt: query all hosts that ran npm install/update against the mastra or @mastra scope or that resolved easy-day-js@1.11.21 or 1.11.22 between 2026-06-16 and 2026-06-17; pivot to UC2/UC3/UC5 to confirm second-stage and persistence.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "setup.cjs" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\easy-day-js\", "easy-day-js/setup.cjs")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has "setup.cjs" and CommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mastra npm Supply Chain easy-day-js Postinstall Dropper
id: a1f8c3d4-7b2e-4f9a-8c5d-1e6b9f2a3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the easy-day-js@1.11.22 postinstall hook spawning the obfuscated setup.cjs dropper via Node.js with --no-warnings.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
  - https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046
author: ThreatHunting-Now
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1546.016
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\node.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'setup.cjs'
      - '--no-warnings'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Benign npm packages whose postinstall happens to be named setup.cjs and invoke node with --no-warnings (uncommon)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR */node) OR @process.executable.path:(*\\node.exe OR */node)) (@CommandLine:(*setup.cjs* AND *--no-warnings*) OR @process.command_line:(*setup.cjs* AND *--no-warnings*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$|\/node$/i CommandLine=/setup\.cjs/i CommandLine=/--no-warnings/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Mastra C2 beacon: node.exe to Hostwinds 23.254.164.92:8000 / .123:443 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the setup.cjs dropper or its second-stage tasking client connecting to the attacker-controlled Hostwinds infrastructure used by the Mastra campaign. Single-event alerting on the two confirmed C2 IPs. Rationale: Two attacker-controlled IPs (23.254.164.92:8000 fetch, 23.254.164.123:443 beacon) and two Hostwinds DNS names published verbatim by Microsoft Threat Intelligence. Single-IOC match is high-fidelity because the IPs sit on a low-reputation hosting provider and were freshly stood up for this campaign. The DNS join catches detections even when the proxy resolves IPs locally. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal threat-intel sandbox or red team detonating the dropper for research
  • Security researcher pivoting against the Hostwinds IP space from a corporate host
  • A different legitimate Hostwinds-hosted customer reusing the same IP after take-down (low — IPs were burned)
  • DNS scanner / passive DNS collector hitting the hwsrv-132778x hostnames
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") or isempty(InitiatingProcessFileName)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process (expect node.exe), pull bytes-up/down to gauge whether the second-stage payload was retrieved or implant beacons completed; enrich the IP via passive DNS for any other Hostwinds C2 names. 2) Contain: block 23.254.164.0/24 at the egress proxy / firewall, sinkhole the two hwsrv-132778[56].hostwindsdns.com domains, isolate any host that connected. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source host to UC1 (setup.cjs execution), UC3 (NvmProtocal Run key), UC5 (wallet/browser data access); broaden lookback to 30d to catch any earlier connection from CI runners.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
  | where RemotePort in (8000, 443)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | where AdditionalFields has_any ("hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, AdditionalFields, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| sort by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where DestinationIP in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where Name in~ ("hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where DstIpAddr in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Mastra implant Windows persistence: NvmProtocal Run key + NodePackages drop AIInstallation High
Detects the cross-platform tasking implant installing login persistence on Windows by writing the NvmProtocal value under HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run and/or dropping protocal.cjs under C:\ProgramData\NodePackages\. Rationale: Microsoft Table 2 names the persistence artifact 'NvmProtocal' (note the typo — 'Protocal' vs 'Protocol') under C:\ProgramData\NodePackages\ — both strings are unique enough that any hit is essentially confirmed malicious. The typo is a high-fidelity anchor because legitimate NVM uses 'Protocol' or no such key at all. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18046
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user installs a legitimate NVM4W variant that coincidentally writes a similarly named key (extremely unlikely with the 'Protocal' typo)
  • Security tooling re-detonating the implant in an analysis VM
  • Forensic acquisition tooling reading the key (would show ActionType=RegistryQuery, not Set/Created — already filtered)
  • Manual analyst remediation activity touching the path after IR is underway
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("setup.exe","msiexec.exe") or RegistryValueData has "protocal.cjs"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the value data to confirm it points at protocal.cjs; correlate to the initiating process (expect node.exe, sometimes powershell.exe); hash protocal.cjs and compare against the published five SHA256s. 2) Contain: isolate the host, delete the Run value and the NodePackages folder, kill the implant process, rotate any credentials/tokens/cookies accessible to that user. 3) Hunt: query ImageLoadEvents / DllInjection for reflective .NET loads from node.exe in the prior 24h; check for the equivalent macOS LaunchAgent ~/Library/NodePackages/com.nvm.protocal.plist and Linux ~/.config/systemd/nvmconf/nvmconf.service across the fleet.
union
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValueName =~ "NvmProtocal"
        or RegistryValueData has_any (@"\ProgramData\NodePackages\", "protocal.cjs")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where FileName =~ "protocal.cjs" or FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\NodePackages\"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| sort by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValue =~ "NvmProtocal" or RegistryValueData has_any (@"\ProgramData\NodePackages\", "protocal.cjs")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ "protocal.cjs" or TargetFilePath has @"\ProgramData\NodePackages\"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Mastra implant credential access: node.exe reading crypto wallet extensions / browser History AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the second-stage tasking implant inventorying the 166 cryptocurrency wallet browser-extension IDs and copying browser History/Login Data into temp paths prefixed with 'browser-hist-'. Non-browser Node.js process touching browser profile data is the key signal. Rationale: Article confirms node.exe inventories 166 wallet extension IDs across Chrome/Edge/Brave profiles, copies History SQLite into temp paths prefixed 'browser-hist-' (verbatim). Non-browser process reading browser secret stores is normally rare; the node.exe-as-initiator pivot makes this a tight detection on developer endpoints.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1005 T1217
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Electron-based developer tools (VS Code extensions, GitHub Desktop, Slack desktop) reading their own Chromium profile under User Data — distinguish via the Local Extension Settings/History/Login Data sub-paths
  • Browser-history exporters (e.g. browsing-history-export CLI) that some devs run via node
  • Backup/sync tools written in Node that snapshot the browser profile
  • Penetration-testing tooling on engagement laptops
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("Code.exe","code.exe","GitHubDesktop.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","Discord.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent of node.exe (expect npm postinstall lineage from UC1, not VS Code / Electron); enumerate which extension IDs / which browser profile were touched; check for outbound POSTs to UC2 IPs within 5 minutes of the access. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate node tree, rotate seed phrases / hardware-wallet PINs / exchange API keys / 2FA seeds for every wallet found, expire all browser sessions for that user. 3) Hunt: correlate the user's Okta/Entra sign-ins and CEX exchange logins for the prior 7d; check for fund-movement events; pivot to UC2 for exfil confirmation and any HTTPS POST with the legacy IE8 User-Agent.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FolderPath has_any (@"\User Data\Default\Local Extension Settings\",
                              @"\User Data\Default\Extensions\",
                              @"\User Data\Default\History",
                              @"\User Data\Default\Login Data",
                              @"\User Data\Default\Cookies",
                              @"\Brave-Browser\User Data\",
                              @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\"))
   or FileName startswith "browser-hist-"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| sort by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\User Data\Default\Local Extension Settings\",
                                  @"\User Data\Default\Extensions\",
                                  @"\User Data\Default\History",
                                  @"\User Data\Default\Login Data",
                                  @"\User Data\Default\Cookies")
   or TargetFileName startswith "browser-hist-"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) (@TargetFilename:(*\\User\ Data\\Default\\Local\ Extension\ Settings\\* OR *\\User\ Data\\Default\\Extensions\\* OR *\\User\ Data\\Default\\History* OR *\\User\ Data\\Default\\Login\ Data* OR *\\User\ Data\\Default\\Cookies*) OR @TargetFilename:*\\browser-hist-*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i (TargetFileName=/\\User Data\\.*\\(Local Extension Settings|Extensions|History|Login Data|Cookies)/i OR TargetFileName=/\\browser-hist-/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

Mastra implant discovery: PowerShell child of node.exe running Get-StartApps / Get-AppxPackage AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the implant's host-fingerprinting step: enumerating installed software via Get-StartApps, Get-AppxPackage, and registry Uninstall keys in rapid succession spawned as a child of node.exe. Rationale: Microsoft's Phase 6 reconstruction names the exact three enumeration mechanisms (Get-StartApps, Get-AppxPackage, registry Uninstall) used by the implant for victim profiling. PowerShell as a child of node.exe is rare in normal developer use; combined with these three discovery commands, this is essentially confirmation of the implant being active.
ATT&CKT1518 T1518.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An npm package's postinstall that legitimately queries installed apps via PowerShell (rare but exists for some Windows-targeting npm modules)
  • node-based system inventory tools (e.g. systeminformation library wrappers) that shell out for AppX data
  • DevOps tooling that uses node to drive PowerShell-based Windows configuration checks
  • Electron app updater that queries Get-AppxPackage to detect Store-installed versions
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "systeminformation" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("electron.exe","Code.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full command line and parent node.exe command line; check if setup.cjs or a randomly named .js was the parent (UC1 lineage); look at the next 60 seconds of process events on the same host for follow-on PS reading browser data or registry hives. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill node and powershell trees, quarantine any .js dropped under temp/AppData. 3) Hunt: pivot on UC2 (C2 IPs) and UC5 (wallet/browser access) for the same DeviceId; check whether the user has any privileged AD / cloud roles and freeze them pending review.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-StartApps","Get-AppxPackage",@"\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| sort by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Get-StartApps","Get-AppxPackage",@"\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Crypto Clipper uses Tor and worm-like propagation for persistence and control

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-17 16 use cases 15 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a cryptocurrency clipper campaign that combines clipboard theft, wallet replacement, Tor-based communications, and worm-like propagation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] curl SOCKS5 to localhost:9050 .onion C2 beacon · [LLM] Beacon/screenshot/payload C2 endpoint requested via Tor SOCKS5 · [LLM] Loopback connection to 127.0.0.1:9050 from non-Tor process · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] 'cfile' EVAL backdoor payload dropped by script interpreter
Renamed Tor binary 'ugate.exe' launched by WScript with hidden window AIInstallation High
Hunts for the CryptoBandits clipper launching its bundled Tor proxy renamed to ugate.exe. The article calls out the renamed binary, hidden-window flag and a ~60s bootstrap delay, all spawned by script interpreters. Rationale: Article §Execution names the renamed Tor binary ugate.exe explicitly and the C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char> staging folder. Block 1 (schtasks) shows the same path. Anchored on both the binary name and the path so renames in either dimension are caught. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team using bundled Tor proxies for traffic anonymization tests
  • Privacy-focused power user dropping a renamed Tor portable in their profile (unlikely under Public\Documents)
  • Custom packaged software shipping a helper named ugate.exe (verify signature)
  • Penetration test using portable Tor binaries staged via WScript
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the ugate.exe SHA256 and compare against the article IOCs; check parent WScript command line for a .js script under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\. Step 2 — Contain: isolate device via MDE machine action, kill ugate.exe + parent wscript.exe, block the SHA256 at AV, remove scheduled tasks under the 4-6 char name pattern. Step 3 — Hunt: DeviceFileEvents for all writes under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\, DeviceNetworkEvents for curl --socks5-hostname localhost:9050 connections, and DeviceEvents ActionType=='AntivirusExclusionUpdated' for the staging folder.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "ugate.exe"
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "ugate.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\Users\Public\Documents\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\ugate.exe"
   or (ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and CommandLine has "ugate.exe")
| where CommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Documents\" or NewProcessName has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Renamed Tor Binary ugate.exe From Public Documents (CryptoBandits)
id: 7c4c1a8b-4e1c-4f2e-9b1a-7e3a6d2c0a1f
description: Detects launch of a renamed Tor binary (ugate.exe) from a per-user Public\Documents staging folder used by the CryptoBandits crypto clipper.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/crypto-clipper-uses-tor-worm-like-propagation-for-persistence-control/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1090.003
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ugate.exe'
    Image|contains: '\Users\Public\Documents\'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\ugate.exe OR *\UGATE.EXE) OR (@ParentImage:(*\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe) AND @CommandLine:*ugate.exe*)) @Image:(*\Users\Public\Documents\* OR *\users\public\documents\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\ugate\.exe$/i OR (ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe/i CommandLine=/ugate\.exe/i)
| regex("\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\Documents\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="ugate.exe" OR (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND Processes.process="*ugate.exe*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where like(process_path,"%\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\%") OR match(process,"(?i)ugate\.exe")

curl SOCKS5 to localhost:9050 .onion C2 beacon AICommand & Control High
Detects the clipper's egress channel: curl.exe invoked with --socks5-hostname pointing at localhost:9050 to reach a .onion C2. Article Block 2 and Block 3 confirm this exact cmdline shape. Rationale: Block 2 and Block 3 in the article give the literal curl + socks5-hostname + localhost:9050 + .onion combination. Endpoint enrichment maps to article §C2 (/route.php, /recvf.php, /stub.php). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/ • https://2019.www.torproject.org/docs/tor-manual.html.en
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher fetching a known .onion mirror through a local Tor SOCKS5
  • Privacy-tooling vendor agent (Brave/Tor Browser bundle) using curl test scripts
  • Red-team exercise simulating hidden-service C2
  • Threat-intel analyst pulling IOC feeds from a .onion repository
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("torbrowser-install.exe","tor-browser.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Tor Browser\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the full curl command (HTTP method, endpoint, GUID/GEIP body), confirm parent is wscript/cscript or ugate.exe, pivot to DeviceFileEvents for a 'cfile' write. Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, kill curl.exe + parent script, terminate any ugate.exe, remove the two scheduled tasks under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\. Step 3 — Hunt: list every host with curl.exe whose parent is wscript/cscript in the last 30 days; pivot DeviceFileEvents to all 'cfile' creations and screenshot drops in the staging folder.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "curl.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--socks5-hostname", ":9050", ".onion")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "--socks5-hostname" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("localhost:9050","127.0.0.1:9050"))
| extend Endpoint = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/route.php", "beacon",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/recvf.php", "screenshot-upload",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/stub.php",  "payload-download",
    "other")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Endpoint, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
| where CommandLine has_all ("--socks5-hostname", ":9050", ".onion")
| extend Endpoint = case(
    CommandLine has "/route.php", "beacon",
    CommandLine has "/recvf.php", "screenshot-upload",
    CommandLine has "/stub.php",  "payload-download",
    "other")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, Endpoint, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Worm scheduled-task created from Public\Documents 5-char staging folder AIInstallation High
Detects schtasks creating an indefinite task whose name and XML body live under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\<5char>.xml — the persistence mechanism the article shows for both the worm and clipper components. Rationale: Verbatim from article Block 1 (Microsoft's own AH query). The 5-char folder/file naming + C:\Users\Public\Documents prefix is article-specific and not seen for legitimate scheduled tasks. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT-provisioning script using a randomized short task name (rare — IT typically uses descriptive names)
  • Internal red-team mimicking the CryptoBandits TTP
  • SCCM custom action staging XML jobs (typically under ProgramData, not Public)
  • Backup tool dropping a temporary task config (typically under %TEMP%)
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the XML the task references (DeviceFileEvents for the path), look at the wrapped command — typically wscript.exe firing one of the two JS files in the same folder. Step 2 — Contain: schtasks /Delete /TN <name> /F, isolate device, kill any wscript/cscript holding the JS open. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate every schtasks /create in the last 30 days with the 5-char + Public\Documents pattern; pivot to DeviceEvents AntivirusExclusionUpdated and DeviceFileEvents for the staging folder.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)schtasks\s+/create\s+/tn\s+[a-z]{4,6}\s+/xml\s+C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\[a-z]{4,6}\\[a-z]{4,6}\.xml\s+/f"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)schtasks\s+/create\s+/tn\s+[a-z]{4,6}\s+/xml\s+C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\[a-z]{4,6}\\[a-z]{4,6}\.xml\s+/f"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Defender AV folder/path exclusion targeting Public\Documents staging AIInstallation Medium
Detects the worm's defense-evasion step where it adds AV exclusions for its staging folder and the Windows binaries it abuses (Behavior:Win64/PathExclusion.STA family is the Defender signature). Rationale: Article §Execution: 'It excludes staging folders and Windows binaries used in the execution of the stealer component'; Defender lab signatures Behavior:Win64/PathExclusion.STA confirm. We anchor on Add-MpPreference + the specific binary/path strings the article calls out. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-exclusions • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Help-desk technician temporarily excluding a problematic developer folder
  • Custom anti-malware deployment script that excludes a known-good vendor binary
  • IT vendor MSP onboarding script adding broad path exclusions
  • Software installer that registers itself as an exclusion (legitimate vendors rarely under Public\Documents)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm exclusion target matches staging folder pattern; pull the parent of the powershell.exe to see if it was a script (wscript/cscript) or interactive. Step 2 — Contain: remove the exclusion (Remove-MpPreference), full-scan the staging folder, isolate device. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate Add-MpPreference across fleet for Public\Documents paths; correlate with curl SOCKS5 detection and ugate.exe detection on the same host.
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "Add-MpPreference"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Users\Public\Documents\", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "curl.exe", "ugate.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="PSExclusion", ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ("AntivirusExclusionUpdated","AsrPathExclusionAdded")
  | where AdditionalFields has_any (@"\Users\Public\Documents\", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "curl.exe", "ugate.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source=ActionType, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where CommandLine has "Add-MpPreference"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\Users\Public\Documents\","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","ugate.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WScript/CScript executing JS from Public\Documents 5-char folder AIExploitation High
Hunts for the two dual-layer-obfuscated JavaScript payloads (worm + stealer) the article drops under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\<5char>.js. WScript/CScript executing JS from this path is non-business. Rationale: Article §Execution (figure 4 'omoho' example) confirms the 5-char folder + 5-char .js filename under C:\Users\Public\Documents. WScript executing JS from this path has no legitimate business use. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom helpdesk JS tool staged under Public Documents by an old IT script
  • Legacy LOB application that ships .js helpers in Public (rare)
  • IT admin manually testing a JScript file in Public
  • Vendor installer leaving cleanup .js in Public (typically under ProgramData)
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the JS file from the staging folder, capture SHA256, look for double-layer obfuscation and WScript.Shell + ActiveXObject calls. Step 2 — Contain: kill wscript/cscript, delete the staging folder, isolate the device, remove scheduled tasks pointing at it. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot DeviceFileEvents for FileCreated under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\ in the last 30 days; cross-reference with hosts that mounted removable media (DeviceEvents PnPDeviceConnected).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\[a-z]{4,6}\\[a-z]{4,6}\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\[a-z]{4,6}\\[a-z]{4,6}\.js"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

USB-borne .lnk worm: shortcut files mass-created on removable media AIDelivery Medium
Detects the worm's propagation step where it iterates files on a removable USB volume, hides the originals, and creates same-named .lnk shortcuts pointing to the worm executable. Rationale: Article §Initial access: the .lnk worm 'scans the USB device for common document files... hides the original files, and creates additional .lnk shortcut files with the same file names.' The mass-create burst pattern (≥5 .lnk in 5 min, outside normal shortcut homes) catches the propagation step. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1091/
ATT&CKT1091 T1547.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User extracts a ZIP containing multiple .lnk shortcuts
  • Software installer dropping menu shortcuts (filtered by parent process)
  • Cloud sync agent (OneDrive, Dropbox) materialising shortcut-like placeholders
  • Backup tool restoring a folder full of .lnk files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe","OneDrive.exe","setup.exe","7z.exe","7zG.exe","WinRAR.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: inspect the .lnk targets — CryptoBandits shortcuts point at the worm EXE staged elsewhere on the same device; check if the same DeviceName had a recent removable-media mount event. Step 2 — Contain: isolate device, quarantine the USB volume, delete the malicious .lnk batch and restore hidden originals, kill the worm process. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate all hosts that have written ≥5 .lnk to removable media in the last 30 days; pivot to scheduled-task creation and ugate.exe detections on those hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".lnk"
| where FolderPath !has @"\Programs\" and FolderPath !has @"\Recent\" and FolderPath !has @"\Start Menu\" and FolderPath !has @"\Roaming\Microsoft\Office\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe")
| summarize LnkCount = dcount(FileName), Sample = make_set(FileName,10), Folders = make_set(FolderPath,5) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where LnkCount >= 5
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension =~ "lnk"
| where TargetFilePath !has @"\Programs\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Recent\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Start Menu\"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe")
| summarize LnkCount = dcount(TargetFileName), Sample = make_set(TargetFileName,10) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where LnkCount >= 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*.lnk OR *.LNK) -@TargetFilename:(*\Programs\* OR *\Recent\* OR *"\\Start Menu\\"*) -@Image:(*\explorer.exe OR *\msiexec.exe OR *\setup.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\.lnk$/i
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\(Programs|Recent|Start Menu)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(explorer|msiexec|setup)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=5m)], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=lnk_count))
| lnk_count >= 5
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as distinct_lnk from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created Filesystem.file_name="*.lnk" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_lnk >= 5 AND NOT match(file_path,"(?i)\\\\(Programs|Recent|Start Menu)\\\\")
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as distinct_lnk from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created Filesystem.file_name="*.lnk" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_lnk >= 5 AND NOT match(file_path,"(?i)\\\\(Programs|Recent|Start Menu)\\\\")
WMI Win32_Process query used as Task Manager anti-analysis gate AIExploitation Medium
Detects the clipper's anti-analysis check — querying Win32_Process via WMI/WScript and bailing if taskmgr.exe is present. The specific combination (WScript parent + WMI Win32_Process query) is article-distinctive. Rationale: Article §Defense evasion: 'querying the Win32_Process WMI class and terminating execution if Task Manager is detected.' The WScript→WMIC→Win32_Process chain is the on-disk projection of the in-memory ActiveX query.
ATT&CKT1518.001 T1047
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT diagnostic JScript using WMIC to enumerate processes
  • Sysadmin-authored WScript reporting tool
  • Legacy LOB app polling for a competing process
  • Vendor uninstaller checking if its own helper is running
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm parent JS file lives under C:\Users\Public\Documents\<5char>\; pull the JS contents for the BIP39 regex strings or 'Tor' references. Step 2 — Contain: kill wscript/cscript, delete the staging folder, terminate ugate.exe, remove scheduled tasks, isolate device. Step 3 — Hunt: search 30 days back for the same wscript→wmic→Win32_Process pattern across the fleet; cross-correlate with curl SOCKS5 and ugate.exe detections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| where FileName =~ "wmic.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_Process","process get","process where")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Win32_Process","process get","process where")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WScript-Spawned WMIC Win32_Process Enumeration (CryptoBandits Anti-Analysis)
id: 6b9e8a5d-1f70-49b4-90c4-1c2a9d0e7d34
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawning wmic.exe to query Win32_Process — the anti-analysis gate the CryptoBandits clipper uses to bail when Task Manager is open.
references:

    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Win32_Process'
      - 'process get'
      - 'process where'
  condition: selection

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe) @Image:(*\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.exe) @CommandLine:(*Win32_Process* OR *"process get"* OR *"process where"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\wmic\.exe$/i
| regex("(Win32_Process|process\\s+get|process\\s+where)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process,"(?i)(Win32_Process|process\s+get)") AND match(parent_process,"(?i)C:\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\Documents\\\\")
Beacon/screenshot/payload C2 endpoint requested via Tor SOCKS5 AICommand & Control High
Higher-fidelity slice of the curl-Tor detection that anchors on the article's three specific C2 endpoints (/route.php, /recvf.php, /stub.php) and classifies the action — beacon, screenshot upload, or payload download. Rationale: Article §C2 lists /route.php (beacon + EVAL command retrieval), /recvf.php (screenshot upload), /stub.php (payload download). These three endpoints are the article's specific C2 fingerprint and won't fire on legitimate Tor traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1041/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher poking the CryptoBandits C2 directly
  • Sandbox/detonation host running the sample for analysis
  • Internal purple-team reusing the campaign infra for a tabletop
  • CTF or training environment replaying the IOCs
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Detonation\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Sandbox\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the full request, decide which lifecycle stage the host is at (beacon, screenshot, payload). A /stub.php hit means the EVAL backdoor will likely fire next. Step 2 — Contain: isolate device, kill curl + parent script + ugate.exe, delete the staging folder and cfile, remove scheduled tasks. Step 3 — Hunt: search the past 90 days for any host that ever made a request to these three endpoint paths; pivot DeviceFileEvents for 'cfile' creation and screenshot drops.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "curl.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".onion"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/route.php","/recvf.php","/stub.php")
| extend Action = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/route.php", "beacon-or-EVAL",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/recvf.php", "screenshot-exfil",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/stub.php",  "payload-download",
    "other")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Action, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".onion"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/route.php","/recvf.php","/stub.php")
| extend Action = case(
    CommandLine has "/route.php", "beacon-or-EVAL",
    CommandLine has "/recvf.php", "screenshot-exfil",
    CommandLine has "/stub.php",  "payload-download",
    "other")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, Action, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: curl Request to CryptoBandits C2 Endpoint over Tor
id: f01e3a92-3b21-4d11-89f4-2c4e5b6a7c88
description: Detects curl.exe issuing a request to one of the CryptoBandits C2 endpoints (/route.php, /recvf.php, /stub.php) hosted on a .onion service.
references:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\curl\.exe$/i

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="curl.exe" Processes.process IN ("*route.php*","*recvf.php*","*stub.php*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval action=case(match(process,"(?i)route\.php"),"beacon",match(process,"(?i)recvf\.php"),"screenshot-upload",match(process,"(?i)stub\.php"),"payload-download") | where match(process,"(?i)\.onion")
'cfile' EVAL backdoor payload dropped by script interpreter AIActions on Objectives High
Article-named drop file: a single file literally called 'cfile' (no extension) is written to disk to hold the EVAL JScript payload downloaded over Tor. This file name + the WScript parent is a near-unique fingerprint. Rationale: Article §C2: 'A file named cfile is created on the infected system as an output for payload hosted on the C2 domain' and the CheckC2Command function EVALs its contents. The bare filename 'cfile' written by a script host is essentially never legitimate. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer accidentally naming a config 'cfile' (rare; usually no extension)
  • Linux-port build tool dropping config helpers (e.g. CMake artifacts have extensions)
  • Vendor tool with a coincidentally-named cache
  • CTF / sandbox replay of the same campaign
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read cfile contents — if it parses as JScript it's the EVAL payload; capture and submit to malware analysis. Step 2 — Contain: kill wscript/cscript/curl/ugate.exe, isolate device, delete cfile and the staging folder, remove scheduled tasks. Step 3 — Hunt: search 90 days for any host that ever wrote a file literally named cfile; pivot to network egress on those hosts for the C2 endpoints.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName =~ "cfile"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","ugate.exe")
   or FolderPath has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName =~ "cfile"
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","ugate.exe")
   or TargetFilePath has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 2bb47e91-58cd-4a13-915c-3a9d1f8b7c01
description: Detects a file literally named 'cfile' (no extension) being created by a script interpreter or curl — the on-disk holder for EVAL JScript fetched from the CryptoBandits C2.

Loopback connection to 127.0.0.1:9050 from non-Tor process AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any process other than a legitimate Tor client establishing a SOCKS5 connection to localhost:9050 — the article's clipper does this from curl.exe + the renamed ugate.exe. Rationale: Article §Defense evasion: 'routing communication over localhost:9050'. Loopback to 9050 from curl.exe or a renamed binary like ugate.exe is the indelible network shape, even when the .onion target rotates. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/001/ • https://2019.www.torproject.org/docs/tor-manual.html.en
ATT&CKT1090.001 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Tor Browser bundle on a developer/researcher workstation
  • SecureDrop client or other privacy tooling
  • Penetration-test toolkit running a Tor SOCKS proxy
  • Anti-censorship browser plugin
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Tor Project" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Tor Browser\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm initiating process is not a sanctioned Tor build; check its parent (WScript? CScript?) and binary location (Public\Documents?). Step 2 — Contain: kill the initiating process and any ugate.exe, isolate device, remove staging folder and scheduled tasks. Step 3 — Hunt: across the fleet, list all distinct processes that have made 9050 loopback connections in the last 90 days; non-Tor entries are suspect.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and RemotePort == 9050
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tor.exe","firefox.exe","tor-browser.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and DstPortNumber == 9050
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("tor.exe","firefox.exe","tor-browser.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Tor Process Connecting to Local SOCKS5 9050 (CryptoBandits)
id: 8d5b1c44-3f1c-4f72-92ba-4e7a8d0c6f44

#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=127.0.0.1 RemotePort=9050

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip="127.0.0.1" All_Traffic.dest_port=9050 by All_Traffic.src_ip All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(process_name,"(?i)^(tor|tor-browser|firefox)\.exe$")
Run-key autostart written by WScript from Public Documents staging AIInstallation Medium
Detects the backup persistence path the worm/clipper takes when scheduled tasks are removed: writing a Run-key autostart that points back at the staging folder under Public\Documents. Rationale: Article describes scheduled tasks as primary persistence; the reviewer's suggested Run-key backup persistence is consistent with the dual-component architecture and staging-folder pattern (Public\Documents\<5char>, ugate.exe). Anchoring on both the destination data string and a script-host parent narrows to article-shaped persistence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor installer writing a Run key for an updater (data won't reference Public\Documents)
  • Custom JS-based deployment script that writes a Run key for a corporate tool
  • Legacy LOB app persisting itself via WScript helper
  • Anti-virus or backup tool autostart registration
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","OneDrive.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the RegistryValueData — does it reference the 5-char Public\Documents folder or ugate.exe; check DeviceFileEvents for the referenced binary. Step 2 — Contain: remove the Run-key value, kill any running ugate.exe/wscript.exe, delete the staging folder and scheduled tasks, isolate device. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate Run/RunOnce additions across the fleet whose data string references Public\Documents, .js, or ugate.exe in the last 30 days.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\Users\Public\Documents\", "ugate.exe", ".js")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\Users\Public\Documents\", "ugate.exe", ".js")
   or ActingProcessName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Run-Key Autostart Written by WScript or Pointing at Public Documents Staging (CryptoBandits)
id: 47fa1c20-7c6d-41a6-b3fb-9c3b1d2a4f55
description: Detects Run/RunOnce registry value being written either by a script interpreter or with data referencing the CryptoBandits staging folder (Public\Documents\<5char>) or its renamed Tor binary (ugate.exe).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/crypto-clipper-uses-tor-worm-like-propagation-for-persistence-control/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\CurrentVersion\Run'
      - '\CurrentVersion\RunOnce'
  selection_match_data:
    Details|contains:
      - '\Users\Public\Documents\'
      - 'ugate.exe'
  selection_match_proc:
