      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection_path and (selection_match_data or selection_match_proc)
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\CurrentVersion\Run\* OR *\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\* OR *\currentversion\run\*) (@Details:(*\Users\Public\Documents\* OR *ugate.exe* OR *\users\public\documents\*) OR @Image:(*\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe))
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| regex("\\\\CurrentVersion\\\\Run", field=RegObjectName)
| (regex("(?i)(\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\Documents\\\\|ugate\\.exe)", field=RegStringValue) OR ContextImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce*") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where match(registry_value_data,"(?i)(C:\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\Documents\\\\[a-z]{4,6}|ugate\.exe|wscript.*\.js)") OR match(process_name,"(?i)(wscript|cscript)\.exe")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce*") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where match(registry_value_data,"(?i)(C:\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\Documents\\\\[a-z]{4,6}|ugate\.exe|wscript.*\.js)") OR match(process_name,"(?i)(wscript|cscript)\.exe")
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args Installation High
schtasks.exe /create or Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler EventID 4698 with LOLBin actions.
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8") or SHA1 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8") or MD5 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8") or SHA1 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8") or MD5 in~ ("7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7630debd35cac6b7d58c4427695579b3e3a8b1cc462f523234cd6c698882a68c", "a7abf1d9d6686af1cefcd60b17a312e7eb8cfe267def1ec34aeab6128c811630", "23c1e673f315dafa14b73034a90dd3d393a984451ff6601b8be8142be6487b43", "cf9fc891ea5ca5ecd8113ef3e69f6f52ff538b6cccbdaa9559106fc72bc6da30", "100407796028bf3649752d9d2a67a0e4394d752eb8de86daa42920e814f3fae8"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45607", "CVE-2026-45641", "CVE-2026-47652", "CVE-2026-41108", "CVE-2026-45608", "CVE-2026-45634", "CVE-2026-45648", "CVE-2026-47289", "CVE-2026-45657", "CVE-2026-47291")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.

HAPI FHIR XXE: DOCTYPE/ENTITY SYSTEM payload posted to FHIR endpoint (CVE-2026-55471) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP POST/PUT to FHIR API paths whose XML body carries XXE markers (<!DOCTYPE … <!ENTITY … SYSTEM 'file://' or 'http://'). Targets the entry-point of CVE-2026-55471 where attacker-controlled XML is fed to XsltUtilities.saxonTransform with an unhardened Saxon TransformerFactory. Rationale: Article specifies the entry point is XML fed to XsltUtilities.saxonTransform; PoC literally shows '<!DOCTYPE root [' + '<!ENTITY canary SYSTEM "file://..."' + '<!ENTITY % oob SYSTEM "http://..."'. FHIR URL fragments come from standard HAPI deployments. Corroborated via vulnerability.circl.lu GHSA-2F55-G35J-5JMF entry. Cross-checked against: • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2f55-g35j-5jmf
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal Burp/ZAP/Nuclei scans hitting FHIR endpoints with XXE payloads as part of authorized AppSec testing
  • Legitimate FHIR XML payloads that include a benign internal DOCTYPE (rare but possible for IG packages)
  • Health-IT interop tools that embed XSD references via DOCTYPE during conformance testing
  • WAF echo-back / debug logs that quote the original payload back into the log line
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Burp","ZAP","Nuclei","sqlmap","Acunetix") and SourceIP !in ("<known_scanner_ips>")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — Pull the full request body and confirm an external SYSTEM identifier (file://, http://, https://, jar:, netdoc:). Map the destination FHIR endpoint to its backing JVM/container and check whether HAPI FHIR org.hl7.fhir.utilities < 6.9.10 is present. 2) CONTAIN — Block the source IP at the WAF, drop any in-flight session, and add a virtual patch rule that rejects FHIR POST/PUT bodies containing <!DOCTYPE or <!ENTITY. If exploitation confirmed, isolate the FHIR app server and rotate any local secrets the JVM could read. 3) HUNT — Pivot on the source IP across the last 30d for other FHIR endpoints and parameter-entity variants (UC2). Pull DeviceFileEvents on the JVM host for /etc/passwd, application.properties, ~/.aws/credentials reads (UC3). Pull DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound HTTP/DNS from java.exe to the attacker-controlled OOB domain (UC4).
// Defender XDR does not capture HTTP request bodies; pivot is the FHIR endpoint URL hit (DeviceNetworkEvents shows the host:port + URL fragment only). Pair with WAF logs in Sentinel (sentinel_kql below) for body inspection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted" or ActionType == "ConnectionInbound"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/fhir/","/hl7/fhir/","/baseR4/","/baseDstu3/","/StructureDefinition","/ValueSet")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort
| order by Timestamp desc
let FhirPaths = dynamic(["/fhir/","/hl7/fhir/","/baseR4/","/baseDstu3/","/StructureDefinition","/ValueSet","/metadata"]);
let XxeMarkers = dynamic(["<!DOCTYPE","<!ENTITY","SYSTEM \"file:","SYSTEM \"http:","SYSTEM 'file:","SYSTEM 'http:"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where RequestURL has_any (FhirPaths)
| extend BodyCandidates = strcat(tostring(DeviceCustomString1), "|", tostring(DeviceCustomString2), "|", tostring(DeviceCustomString3), "|", tostring(DeviceCustomString4), "|", tostring(DeviceCustomString5), "|", tostring(DeviceCustomString6), "|", tostring(RequestContext), "|", tostring(Message))
| where BodyCandidates has_any (XxeMarkers)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, BodyExcerpt = substring(BodyCandidates, 0, 1024), DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HAPI FHIR XXE Payload in HTTP Body (CVE-2026-55471)
id: 8e2a0c14-9e7f-4d5a-bf3e-5471a55471aa
status: experimental
description: Detects inbound HTTP POST/PUT to FHIR endpoints whose body contains XML External Entity declarations, the entry vector for CVE-2026-55471 in HAPI FHIR XsltUtilities.saxonTransform.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2f55-g35j-5jmf
  - https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method:
      - POST
      - PUT
  selection_path:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/fhir/'
      - '/hl7/fhir/'
      - '/baseR4/'
      - '/baseDstu3/'
      - '/StructureDefinition'
      - '/ValueSet'
  selection_body:
    cs-body|contains:
      - '<!DOCTYPE'
      - '<!ENTITY'
      - 'SYSTEM "file:'
      - 'SYSTEM "http:'
  condition: selection_method and selection_path and selection_body
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate FHIR clients using internal DTDs (rare in modern FHIR XML)
  - Security scanners (Burp, ZAP, Nuclei) testing the same endpoints
level: high
(@http.method:(POST OR PUT)) (@http.url_details.path:(*\/fhir\/* OR *\/hl7\/fhir\/* OR *\/baseR4\/* OR *\/baseDstu3\/* OR *\/StructureDefinition* OR *\/ValueSet*)) (@http.request.body:(*"<!DOCTYPE"* OR *"<!ENTITY"* OR *"SYSTEM \"file:"* OR *"SYSTEM \"http:"*))
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method in ("POST","PUT") (Web.url="*/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/hl7/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/baseR4/*" OR Web.url="*/baseDstu3/*" OR Web.url="*/StructureDefinition*" OR Web.url="*/ValueSet*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.user Web.http_user_agent _raw | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search _raw="*<!DOCTYPE*" OR _raw="*<!ENTITY*SYSTEM*" | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?<xxe_marker><!ENTITY[^>]+SYSTEM\s+[\"'](?:file|http|https|ftp|jar|netdoc|gopher):[^\"']+[\"'])" | where isnotnull(xxe_marker) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method in ("POST","PUT") (Web.url="*/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/hl7/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/baseR4/*" OR Web.url="*/baseDstu3/*" OR Web.url="*/StructureDefinition*" OR Web.url="*/ValueSet*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.user Web.http_user_agent _raw | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search _raw="*<!DOCTYPE*" OR _raw="*<!ENTITY*SYSTEM*" | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?<xxe_marker><!ENTITY[^>]+SYSTEM\s+[\"'](?:file|http|https|ftp|jar|netdoc|gopher):[^\"']+[\"'])" | where isnotnull(xxe_marker) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
HAPI FHIR XXE: parameter-entity (<!ENTITY %) OOB exfil pattern on FHIR endpoint AIExploitation High
Higher-fidelity sibling of the generic DOCTYPE hunt: matches only payloads that declare a parameter entity (<!ENTITY %) with an external SYSTEM identifier, the exact pattern used for blind XXE / SSRF in the article's PoC. Parameter entities are vanishingly rare in benign FHIR traffic. Rationale: Article's PoC uses `<!ENTITY % oob SYSTEM "http://127.0.0.1:port/evil-fhir-xslt-ssrf.dtd">` to set up OOB exfil — the parameter-entity construct (`%`) is the distinguishing signature of XXE-via-DTD attacks and almost never appears in legitimate FHIR XML. Much lower-FP than UC1's generic DOCTYPE/ENTITY hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized AppSec scanning by internal red team / Burp Pro extensions
  • Bug-bounty researcher probing exposed FHIR test environments
  • FHIR conformance test harnesses that embed parameter entities in edge-case test vectors (extremely rare)
  • Researcher proof-of-concepts in pre-prod where the source IP belongs to an internal pentest range
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<internal_appsec_scanner_ips>") and RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Burp","ZAP","Nuclei","sqlmap")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — This signature is high-fidelity; treat any hit as exploitation attempt until proven otherwise. Capture the full Body, the source IP, the targeted FHIR resource path, and the parent JVM hostname. Confirm HAPI FHIR version on the receiver. 2) CONTAIN — Block source IP at WAF immediately. Apply ModSecurity / WAF rule to drop any inbound XML containing `<!ENTITY %` for FHIR endpoints regardless of upgrade status. Snapshot the JVM heap if exploit may have succeeded so artefacts can be retrieved later. 3) HUNT — Pivot to UC4 (java.exe outbound to the OOB callback domain in the SYSTEM URI) and UC3 (java.exe reading sensitive local files). Search the WAF for the same source IP over 30d on any FHIR-shaped path. Cross-check the OOB host/IP against threat-intel feeds and add to the Sentinel ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table.
// Defender XDR has no HTTP body visibility; this detection lives in WAF/proxy logs surfaced through Sentinel. The Defender query below is the host-side companion: JVM serving FHIR that immediately performs an outbound HTTP fetch to a public IP (the parameter-entity callback).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hapi","org.hl7.fhir","tomcat","jetty","spring-boot","wildfly")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let FhirPaths = dynamic(["/fhir/","/hl7/fhir/","/baseR4/","/baseDstu3/","/StructureDefinition","/ValueSet","/metadata"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where RequestURL has_any (FhirPaths)
| extend Body = strcat(tostring(DeviceCustomString1),"|",tostring(DeviceCustomString2),"|",tostring(DeviceCustomString3),"|",tostring(DeviceCustomString4),"|",tostring(DeviceCustomString5),"|",tostring(DeviceCustomString6),"|",tostring(RequestContext),"|",tostring(Message))
| where Body matches regex @"(?i)<!ENTITY\s+%\s+\w+\s+SYSTEM\s+[""'](?:file|http|https|ftp|jar|netdoc|gopher):"
| extend ParamEntity = extract(@"(?i)(<!ENTITY\s+%\s+\w+\s+SYSTEM\s+[""'][^""']+[""'])", 1, Body)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, ParamEntity, BodyExcerpt = substring(Body, 0, 1024)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method in ("POST","PUT") (Web.url="*/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/hl7/fhir/*" OR Web.url="*/baseR4/*" OR Web.url="*/baseDstu3/*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.user _raw | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?<param_entity><!ENTITY\s+%\s+\w+\s+SYSTEM\s+[\"'](?<oob_uri>(?:file|http|https|ftp|jar|netdoc|gopher):[^\"']+)[\"'])" | where isnotnull(param_entity) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | table firstTime, src, dest, url, user, param_entity, oob_uri

JVM serving HAPI FHIR reads sensitive local files (XXE file:// disclosure) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-exploitation file reads by the JVM hosting HAPI FHIR: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/hosts, application.properties, application.yml, cloud credentials, and Kubernetes secrets. Catches the file:// SYSTEM-entity arm of CVE-2026-55471 regardless of whether the inbound WAF caught the payload. Rationale: Article's PoC uses `<!ENTITY canary SYSTEM "file://...">` to read a temp file containing `TOP-SECRET-FHIR-XSLT-CANARY-3f9a17c2`. Real attackers will pivot to /etc/passwd, application.properties (DB creds), and cloud-credential files. JVM as the reader + Java-app-server cmdline narrows scope. Corroborated against vulnerability.circl.lu confirmation of the file-disclosure exploitation primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf
ATT&CKT1005 T1083 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • HAPI FHIR legitimately loading its own application.yml / hapi.properties from its install directory at startup
  • Spring Boot Actuator config refresh reading application config
  • Backup/snapshot tooling that crawls the FHIR app directory and triggers file-access events on config
  • Sysadmin running diagnostic tools (strace, jstack against the JVM) that incidentally surface as the JVM touching these files
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath endswith "hapi.properties" and FolderPath startswith "/opt/hapi-fhir/") and not (FolderPath endswith "application.yml" and FolderPath has "/conf/")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — Confirm the JVM in question is the FHIR app server (check parent process tree, listening ports, classpath). Pull the timestamp of the file read and look ±60s in CommonSecurityLog / Web datamodel for an inbound POST/PUT to a FHIR endpoint (UC1/UC2). 2) CONTAIN — Stop the JVM, snapshot heap + thread dump, isolate the host from network. Rotate every secret the JVM could read (application.properties DB creds, AWS access keys, K8s service-account tokens, SSH keys). 3) HUNT — Run UC4 to look for OOB exfil of the file contents to attacker-controlled domains. Search the same JVM hosts for inbound traffic to FHIR endpoints from the source IP over the past 30d. Apply the WAF virtual-patch from UC2 to every FHIR-fronting WAF.
let SensitivePaths = dynamic(["/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","/etc/hosts","/etc/krb5.conf","application.properties","application.yml","hapi.properties","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.kube/config","/.ssh/id_rsa","web.config","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","java","javaw.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hapi","org.hl7.fhir","hapi-fhir","tomcat","jetty","wildfly","spring-boot")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileOpened")

| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("hapi","org.hl7.fhir","hapi-fhir","tomcat","jetty","wildfly","spring-boot")

status: experimental
description: Java process running HAPI FHIR / a typical Java app server reads sensitive local files (passwd, shadow, application config, cloud creds). Likely XXE file:// disclosure via CVE-2026-55471 if no admin justification exists.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2f55-g35j-5jmf
  - https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1005
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/java'
      - '/javaw'
      - '\java.exe'
      - '\javaw.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'hapi'
      - 'org.hl7.fhir'
      - 'hapi-fhir'
      - 'tomcat'
      - 'jetty'
      - 'wildfly'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/etc/passwd'
      - '/etc/shadow'
      - '/etc/hosts'
      - 'application.properties'
      - 'application.yml'
      - 'hapi.properties'
      - '/.aws/credentials'
      - '/.kube/config'
      - '/.ssh/id_rsa'
      - '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - HAPI FHIR legitimately reading its own application.properties at boot from a known path
  - Spring Boot actuator / config-server polling
level: high
@process.executable.name:(java OR javaw OR java.exe OR javaw.exe) @process.command_line:(*hapi* OR *org.hl7.fhir* OR *hapi-fhir* OR *tomcat* OR *jetty* OR *wildfly* OR *spring-boot*) @file.path:(*\/etc\/passwd* OR *\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/etc\/hosts* OR *application.properties* OR *application.yml* OR *hapi.properties* OR *\/.aws\/credentials* OR *\/.kube\/config* OR *\/.ssh\/id_rsa* OR *\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes.io*)

HAPI FHIR JVM out-of-band callback to non-corporate destination (XXE OOB exfil) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the SSRF / blind-XXE arm of CVE-2026-55471: the FHIR-serving JVM makes an outbound HTTP fetch or DNS lookup to a public destination it has never previously contacted, immediately after an inbound POST/PUT to a FHIR endpoint. Captures both the parameter-entity DTD fetch and the file-content exfil pattern. Rationale: PoC sets up `<!ENTITY % oob SYSTEM "http://127.0.0.1:port/evil-fhir-xslt-ssrf.dtd">` and the JVM resolves it, generating an outbound HTTP request from the Saxon TransformerFactory. Real attackers replace 127.0.0.1 with attacker.com. Anti-join against 30d baseline turns 'JVM made an HTTP request' into 'JVM contacted a destination it never contacted before'. Corroborated against vulnerability.circl.lu confirmation of SSRF primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1071.004 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • HAPI FHIR pulling new external IG (Implementation Guide) packages from a registry (registry.fhir.org, packages.simplifier.net)
  • JVM auto-update / Maven Central / Spring Boot Actuator phoning home
  • Newly-onboarded healthcare partner whose endpoint URL is genuinely contacted for the first time
  • Container image rebuilds that change the destination set seen at runtime
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.fhir.org","packages.simplifier.net","packages2.fhir.org","repo.maven.apache.org","repo1.maven.org","jcenter.bintray.com"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — Confirm the destination domain/IP is not a known FHIR registry (registry.fhir.org, packages.simplifier.net, packages2.fhir.org). Look at the immediate-prior inbound HTTP requests to the JVM (CommonSecurityLog / W3CIISLog within 60s before the outbound) for FHIR endpoint POST/PUT carrying the matching attacker domain in a SYSTEM identifier. 2) CONTAIN — If the destination is an attacker callback, block it at egress firewall + add to ThreatIntelligenceIndicator. Rotate any secrets that may have been leaked over the channel (assume worst case — UC3 enumerates targets). 3) HUNT — Pivot on the attacker destination across all JVM hosts in the estate over the past 30d. Pull the file-read events from UC3 in the same time window. Check whether the attacker domain appears in DNS logs from other hosts (lateral targeting).
let Lookback = 7d;
let Baseline = DeviceNetworkEvents

    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")

    | summarize BaselineHits = count(), BaselineHosts = dcount(DeviceName) by RemoteUrl
    | where BaselineHits > 3 or BaselineHosts > 2;

| join kind=leftanti Baseline on RemoteUrl
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol

Vulnerable HAPI FHIR org.hl7.fhir.utilities < 6.9.10 in software inventory (CVE-2026-55471) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory pivot: lists every host running HAPI FHIR with the vulnerable org.hl7.fhir.utilities Maven artifact (< 6.9.10). Drives patching and tells the SOC which hosts to prioritise for the runtime detections (UC1-UC4) until upgraded. Rationale: Article pins the vulnerable artifact (`ca.uhn.hapi.fhir:org.hl7.fhir.utilities`) and the vulnerable file:line (XsltUtilities.java:61/91/106 in <= 6.9.8). Web search confirmed the fix landed in 6.9.10, so the vulnerable range is < 6.9.10. CveId match is the cleanest inventory pivot and directly drives patch prioritisation + scopes UC1-UC4 to the right hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-2f55-g35j-5jmf • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2f55-g35j-5jmf
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Test / lab hosts intentionally running old HAPI FHIR for compatibility testing
  • Containers pinned to a vulnerable version because of an unrelated downstream dependency conflict — true positive for inventory but not actionable until refactor
  • TVM lag — DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities may not enumerate Java JARs unless the agent indexes them; results may under-report
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — Confirm the host is actually serving FHIR (listening on a FHIR endpoint, not just a build artifact). Capture HAPI FHIR base version + org.hl7.fhir.utilities version. 2) CONTAIN — For internet-facing FHIR hosts: deploy the UC2 WAF rule (block `<!ENTITY %`) as virtual patch. Schedule emergency upgrade to org.hl7.fhir.utilities >= 6.9.10. 3) HUNT — Enable UC1-UC4 with elevated priority for the listed hosts. Backsearch CommonSecurityLog 30d for any FHIR POST/PUT with XXE markers targeting these hosts. Pull DeviceFileEvents for any sensitive-file read by their JVM (UC3).

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Unauthenticated POST to Langflow /api/v1/upload/{flow_id} endpoint (CVE-2026-55450) AIDelivery High
Detects HTTP POST traffic to the deprecated, unauthenticated Langflow upload endpoint exploited by CVE-2026-55450. Hunts the exact URI pattern reachable on the default Langflow port 7860 where any UUID is accepted and no Authorization header is required. Rationale: Article explicitly names POST /api/v1/upload/{flow_id} as the unauthenticated endpoint and shows the curl PoC against port 7860. Cross-checked GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735 advisory and PR #12831 confirming the endpoint path and Langflow default port. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735 • https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/pull/12831
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Langflow users on internal network triggering uploads via the deprecated endpoint pre-1.9.1
  • Internal QA/CI pipelines testing Langflow upload functionality
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Burp) probing the endpoint
  • Authorized red-team / pentest engagements
  • Self-hosted internal Langflow instances reached by power users via curl
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (<internal_qa_subnet>, <vuln_scanner_ips>) and RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Burp")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the target host is running Langflow <1.9.1; check /api/v1/version. Validate source IP — internal/known user vs external/unknown. Pull the response body to see if file_path was disclosed. Step 2 (contain): Block external traffic to TCP/7860 at the perimeter; if Langflow is exposed publicly, push WAF rule blocking POST /api/v1/upload/. Patch to Langflow 1.9.1+. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on source IP for follow-on activity (other Langflow endpoints, scanning behaviour, exfil). Check Langflow cache directory size; look for atypical file extensions written to /var/cache/langflow/ or ~/.cache/langflow/.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 7860 or LocalPort == 7860
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess")
| summarize ConnCount=count(), Hosts=dcount(RemoteIP), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), SampleRemotes=make_set(RemoteIP,25) by DeviceName, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where ConnCount > 5 or Hosts > 1
| order by ConnCount desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/upload/"
| where isempty(RequestClientApplication) or RequestClientApplication !has "Bearer"
| extend FlowId = extract(@"/api/v1/upload/([0-9a-fA-F-]{36})", 1, RequestURL)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, FlowId, ReceivedBytes, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Langflow upload volume spike — disk-exhaustion DoS pattern (CVE-2026-55450) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects abuse of the unauthenticated Langflow upload endpoint at scale — many POSTs to /api/v1/upload/ from one source within a short window, indicating space-exhaustion DoS exploitation. Threshold-based, alerting tier. Rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated users can upload any amount of data to the server without any limitations... can lead to space exhaustion on the server.' Threshold tuned for repeated POSTs to the named endpoint. 1.9.1 patch enforces max_file_size_upload returning HTTP 413, supporting the volume-based abuse model. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735 • https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/pull/12831
ATT&CKT1499.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate bulk-ingest of training documents by power users
  • Langflow CI/CD test suite that exercises the upload endpoint repeatedly
  • Backup/restore tooling re-uploading flow assets
  • Load testing or capacity planning runs
  • Misconfigured client retrying after 413 responses post-patch

| where SourceIP !in (<internal_qa_subnet>, <internal_loadtest_subnet>)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm source IP is external/unknown; check df -h or equivalent on Langflow host for cache-volume utilisation jump. Sample 3-5 of the recorded requests to confirm same URI shape. Step 2 (contain): Rate-limit or block source IP at WAF/firewall; if disk >85%, clear /var/cache/langflow/ (or ~/.cache/langflow/). Restart Langflow if hung. Patch to 1.9.1+. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on source IP for scans against other Langflow paths or other CVE-2026-55450 targets in the org. Search for the same IP hitting other internal AI/ML tooling.

Rapid file growth in Langflow cache directory (CVE-2026-55450 disk exhaustion) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects an unusual rate of file writes under the Langflow cache directory — the artefact of unauthenticated upload abuse. Targets the cache paths named in the advisory (`~/Library/Caches/langflow/`, `~/.cache/langflow/`, `/var/cache/langflow/`). Rationale: Article PoC shows files written to `/Users/ori/Library/Caches/langflow/<flow_id>/<sha>.<ext>`. The advisory describes attackers uploading without limits — disk exhaustion materialises as a burst of writes inside the Langflow cache dir, which is the host-side observable of the attack. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735
ATT&CKT1499.001

Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Langflow bulk ingest of training data
  • Langflow flow import/export operations creating cache assets
  • CI test runs against Langflow
  • Initial Langflow deployment seeding example flows
  • Plugin/extension installs that hydrate the cache directory
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("langflow-import.sh","backup-restore.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect file extensions and sizes in the cache directory — many same-size random-named files or oversized files indicates abuse. Check df -h. Correlate with web access logs (UC above) for inbound POSTs. Step 2 (contain): Stop or restart the Langflow service; clear oversized/unknown files from cache; block source IP at firewall; patch to 1.9.1+. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to network logs for the same time window to attribute the writes to a remote source. Check whether file_path responses were sent back (potential info-leak chain).

Langflow upload response leaks absolute cache path (CVE-2026-55450 info disclosure) AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects HTTP responses from /api/v1/upload/ that include an absolute filesystem path in the response body — the exact information-leak primitive the advisory describes. Pivots on the `file_path` JSON field with `/Caches/langflow/`, `/.cache/langflow/`, or `/var/cache/langflow/` substrings. Rationale: Article: 'in the response, the absolute path of the uploaded file is reported to the attacker, which is an information leak that can assist in chaining other primitives.' PoC response shows `"file_path":"/Users/ori/Library/Caches/langflow/.../...txt"`. Detection keys on the literal JSON field name plus the cache-path substring. Requires WAF/proxy with response-body capture. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735
ATT&CKT1005 T1592.004

Step 1 (triage): Capture the disclosed path; identify Langflow OS/user account from the path (e.g. `/Users/ori` reveals macOS + user `ori`). Determine whether request was authenticated (post-1.9.1) or unauth (pre-patch). Step 2 (contain): If pre-patch and external source, block source IP; expedite upgrade to 1.9.1+. Even post-patch the path still leaks to the owner — consider PR follow-up to return relative paths only. Step 3 (hunt): Search for the disclosed username/home-directory pattern in other attack surfaces — same user enumerated via other Langflow endpoints, SSH attempts, etc.

Correlated Langflow upload burst with cache-directory write spike AIActions on Objectives High
Joins inbound POSTs to /api/v1/upload/{flow_id} with simultaneous file-create bursts under the Langflow cache directory on the same host within a 5-minute window. Confirms the upload→storage chain and rules out unrelated cache churn. Rationale: Reviewer feedback request: tuple-correlate upload burst with cache write burst on same host within 2-5min. Article gives exact URI and exact cache directory pattern; pairing them eliminates background cache churn FPs. Cross-checked PR #12831 — the fix path (save_uploaded_file → folder_name=flow_id_str) confirms the host-side directory shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735 • https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/pull/12831

Successful Langflow /api/* request with missing Authorization header (unauth API access) AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects HTTP 200/201/204 responses to /api/* paths on Langflow hosts where the Authorization header is absent or empty — the broader unauthenticated-access pattern implied by the advisory. Excludes known unauth health endpoints. Rationale: Reviewer feedback + article text: 'Unauthenticated users can upload any amount of data... only network access to Langflow' implies the auth gap may affect other deprecated endpoints. Detection covers /api/ surface area with explicit health-endpoint exclusions and missing-Authorization check. Cross-checked PR #12831 which adds `get_flow` dependency — confirming the missing-auth shape is the root cause class. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x223-p2gf-v735 • https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/pull/12831
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow public docs/static endpoints that legitimately need no auth
  • Reverse proxy that strips Authorization header before forwarding
  • SSO/OIDC flows using cookies rather than Bearer tokens
  • Front-end fetches hitting backend with session cookies
  • Internal monitoring probes hitting undocumented unauth endpoints
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (<internal_monitoring_subnet>) and not(Paths has_any ("/api/v1/docs","/api/v1/openapi.json","/api/v1/auto_login"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm Langflow version (<1.9.1 is vulnerable). Enumerate the specific /api/ paths hit — cross-check against Langflow source for which require auth. Identify source IP attribution. Step 2 (contain): If unauth endpoints other than the known exclusions are reachable externally, restrict at WAF/firewall or via reverse-proxy auth gate. Upgrade to 1.9.1+ which adds get_flow auth dependency. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot source IP and look for follow-on actions — upload attempts, flow enumeration, credential probing on adjacent services.

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/" and not(RequestURL has_any ("/api/v1/health","/api/v1/ping","/api/v1/version","/api/v1/login","/api/v1/auto_login"))
| where toint(coalesce(DeviceCustomString1, "0")) in (200,201,204) or RequestContext has_any ("200","201","204")
| where isempty(RequestClientApplication) or RequestClientApplication !has "Bearer" and RequestClientApplication !has "Cookie"
| summarize HitCount=count(), Paths=make_set(RequestURL,25), Hosts=dcount(DestinationHostName) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where HitCount > 3

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News

An unknown threat actor has been observed leveraging paid or promoted posts on legitimate news websites to drum up buzz for their warez, according to new findings from Check Point Research. The threat actor also has at their disposal a dedicated WordPress phishing page that acts as the central hub, alongside GitHub and SourceForge projects promoted by fake accounts, a YouTube channel, and a

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Crypto 'sniper bot' / Aviator Predictor lure download-and-execute from SourceForge or GitHub · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Crypto 'sniper bot' / Aviator Predictor lure download-and-execute from SourceForge or GitHub AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the Check Point Rust clipper campaign by correlating downloads of executables from SourceForge or GitHub whose filenames match the campaign's specific social-engineering lures (Solana/Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, crash-game predictors) with subsequent first execution from a user-writable path. The SHA256 join between the file-drop and process-execution events makes this article-specific rather than catching any crypto-themed tool a user happens to run. Rationale: The article explicitly names Solana sniper bots, Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, and crash-game predictors as the lure themes, with SourceForge and GitHub as the named distribution platforms — the FileOriginUrl + lure-token correlation ties endpoint detection back to the campaign's specific social-engineering hooks. Cross-checked The Hacker News and InfotechLead coverage and the clip.gif demo (showing the Notepad btc_wallet → wallet-app clipboard substitution) for behavioral confirmation; no public SHA256/wallet IOCs were available at search time, so this is a hunting-tier behavioral query. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/crypto-clipper-campaign-abuses-fake.html • https://infotechlead.com/security/cybercriminals-manipulate-github-youtube-and-virustotal-to-spread-crypto-stealing-malware-96613 • https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi-BtcZtH5fovAmDU_naao6gUXxP7z2gbzRS5dh0ihlwxmyvrKEOvVzkGwCndKLmeurQQ9gVebjrJynRkx8dJF858sS7Xqk9OL4diFcjia9zgBeRndSjrH6j_uuPTEzs2izOhZlS6FeCjtZV8IxCw96vTn1CUIx4nLOfpW7Y1FiRvtSdWovorzSgeK5FZfz/s1700-e365/clip.gif
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1608.001 T1583.006 T1657
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crypto-savvy developer running a legitimate open-source Solana sniper bot from GitHub for personal trading
  • Malware analyst or threat researcher detonating a known crypto-clipper sample in a triage VM
  • Sports betting / fantasy analytics desktop tools whose filename literally contains 'predictor' (e.g. 'NFLPredictor.exe')
  • Game-development AI utilities packaged with names like 'CrashPredictor' for in-game economy testing
  • Red-team / purple-team engagement deliberately running the same campaign tooling for detection tuning
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe", "explorer.exe") and FolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\")) and not (ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ ("Microsoft Corporation", "Google LLC", "Mozilla Corporation", "Valve"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the SHA256 from the join and submit to VirusTotal + MalwareBazaar; verify FileOriginUrl resolves to a SourceForge project or GitHub repo with the boosted-but-shallow signals Check Point flagged (very recent commits, single-contributor, fake-looking stars). Ask the user via chat whether they intentionally downloaded a crypto trading or gambling tool. 2) Contain: Isolate the device in Defender/Falcon. Block the SHA256 organisation-wide via custom IOC. Force-reset any crypto wallet credentials the user used on that device and warn the user not to copy-paste wallet addresses until the host is rebuilt — the clipper substitutes addresses silently. 3) Hunt: Pivot org-wide on the SHA256 and the FileOriginUrl host; expand the lure-token regex to scan 60 days of DeviceFileEvents for sibling drops; check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound HTTPS from the binary to the SourceForge/GitHub origin in case of an updater channel.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let LureTokens = dynamic(["sniper","pumpfun","pump.fun","aviator","predictor","solana-bot","solanabot","crash-predictor","crashpredictor"]);
let SuspectOriginHosts = dynamic(["sourceforge.net","sf.net","github.com","github.io","githubusercontent.com","raw.githubusercontent.com"]);
let SuspectDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".msi" or FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".dmg" or FileName endswith ".pkg" or FileName endswith ".app"
    | where isnotempty(FileOriginUrl)
    | where tolower(FileOriginUrl) has_any (SuspectOriginHosts)
    | extend NameLower = tolower(FileName)
    | where NameLower has_any (LureTokens)
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DroppedFolder = FolderPath, DroppedName = FileName, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\", @"\Public\", "/Users/", "/Applications/", "/tmp/")
| join kind=inner SuspectDrops on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.SHA256 == $right.SHA256
| where Timestamp >= DropTime
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, DropTime)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, DropTime, DelayMinutes, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let LureRegex = @"(?i)(sniper|pump[\.\-_]?fun|aviator|predictor|solana[\-_]?bot|crash[\-_]?predictor)";
let UserPathRegex = @"(?i)\\(Users|Downloads|AppData|Public|Temp)\\";
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex LureRegex
| where TargetProcessName matches regex UserPathRegex
| where TargetProcessName endswith ".exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Crypto Sniper Bot or Aviator Predictor Lure Execution from User-Writable Path
id: 5b8c2f3a-9d41-4e6c-a2b7-1f9c8e3d5072
description: Detects execution of binaries whose names match the Check Point crypto clipper campaign's social-engineering lures (Solana/Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, crash-game predictors) from user-writable paths typically used for downloads.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/crypto-clipper-campaign-abuses-fake.html
  - https://infotechlead.com/security/cybercriminals-manipulate-github-youtube-and-virustotal-to-spread-crypto-stealing-malware-96613
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1657
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    Image|contains:
      - 'sniper'
      - 'pumpfun'
      - 'pump.fun'
      - 'aviator'
      - 'predictor'
      - 'solana-bot'
      - 'solanabot'
      - 'crash-predictor'
      - 'crashpredictor'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Users\'
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Public\'
      - '\Temp\'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate open-source Solana trading bots run by crypto-savvy users
  - Security researchers detonating samples in a sandbox VM
  - Sports analytics or game-AI tools whose filename contains 'predictor'
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Image:(*sniper* OR *Sniper* OR *SNIPER* OR *pumpfun* OR *PumpFun* OR *pump.fun* OR *Pump.Fun* OR *aviator* OR *Aviator* OR *predictor* OR *Predictor* OR *solana-bot* OR *Solana-Bot* OR *solanabot* OR *crash-predictor* OR *Crash-Predictor*)) AND @Image:(*\\Users\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Public\\*) AND -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(sniper|pump[._-]?fun|aviator|predictor|solana[._-]?bot|crash[._-]?predictor)/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(Users|Downloads|AppData|Public|Temp)\\/i
| ImageFileName=/\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen), collect([CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName])])

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.execution
logsource:

detection:

            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'

        Image|endswith:

            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offline

The Hacker News
2026-06-17 18 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A French-speaking attacker broke into a small French automotive business, planted a keylogger, and stole banking and email credentials. Ordinary stuff, until one move near the end. Before his command-and-control server went dark, he installed OpenSSH and Tailscale on a victim's machine, building a way back in that did not run through the C2 at all. When the Havoc server went offline the next
